clue.text: Look out when we come back in starkers

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: starkers is British slang for naked, bare

indicators.note: come back says the word we is turned round to read backwards

explanation.surface: A warning to keep watch for when the naked return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come back' reverses the word we, and 'in' places it inside the slang word for naked; starkers is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are cries telling someone to be careful of danger ahead.

clue.text: Game graduate designed labels

parts.note: a BA (Bachelor of Arts) is a graduate

indicators.note: designed says the letters of the word labels are rearranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A sports fan with a degree created some labels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' looks like a verb about making labels, but it signals the rearrangement that follows the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is a bat-and-ball sport popular in America.

clue.text: Guard in battle fatigues

parts.note: a battle is part of war
fatigues are military dress

explanation.surface: A soldier in combat uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: A wardress is a female prison guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardress is a woman who works as a prison warder.

clue.text: Transported monarch by high-speed train

parts.note: R stands for rex or regina, a monarch
the APT was Britain's Advanced Passenger Train

explanation.surface: A king travels on a fast train.
explanation.walkthrough: The APT was a British high-speed tilting train of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Transported here means carried away with delight, enraptured.

clue.text: A Kentish rebel capturing officer wins praise

indicators.note: capturing says the rebel holds the officer inside him

parts.note: Jack Cade led the 1450 rebellion in Kent
COL is short for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: A rebel from Kent takes an officer prisoner and is applauded for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a revolt from Kent in 1450; 'capturing' says the rebel's name goes around the colonel's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of admiration, a token of acclaim.

clue.text: Devilish group granted representation in London

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches

indicators.note: representation hints at the word granted presented in a new form

explanation.surface: A coven of witches gets permission to appear in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' rearranges GRANTED. Covent Garden is a London district famous for its market and Royal Opera House.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden is a district of central London, home to the opera house.

clue.text: Darn it! That sounds like Mrs Lennon

indicators.note: sounds like says the clue gives a word heard aloud

parts.note: Yoko Ono was married to John Lennon

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance that echoes the name of a Beatle's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Yoko Ono, widow of the Beatle John Lennon.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of dismay or frustration.

clue.text: Supply a horse

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Provide someone with a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply is a quantity or stock of something.

clue.text: Employ engineer? Get on!

parts.note: to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: Should we hire an engineer? Go on!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' means grow old, not proceed.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone is to hire them for work.

clue.text: Fights for bits of food

explanation.surface: Squabbles over leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are brawls or quarrels, and also small leftover morsels at a meal.

clue.text: Nevertheless, nato head gets good service

parts.note: nevertheless means even so

indicators.note: head picks the leading letter of the word nato

explanation.surface: Despite everything, the leader of the alliance gets a decent religious service.
explanation.walkthrough: EVEN SO (nevertheless), the first letter of 'nato' ('head'), and G for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, a form of church worship.

clue.text: Just manage to buckle one's belt?

definitions.text: Just manage to buckle one's belt?

parts.words: Just manage to buckle one's belt?
parts.note: read literally it pictures a stout person barely closing a belt round the waist, the two tips only just touching

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures the two ends of a belt barely touching; the phrase means having only just enough money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to scrape by on a limited income.

clue.text: A brook containing char?

explanation.surface: A stream that might hold a certain fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Char is a trout-like fish, so the surface suggests a stream full of fish; but char also means scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: A burn is a Scottish stream, and to burn is to scorch or blacken by fire.

clue.text: He imprisons two poles within 24 hours

indicators.note: within says the poles are placed inside the span of the day

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
N for north, twice: two poles

explanation.surface: A man locks up two Poles for a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not people but compass points: N and N go 'within' DAY. 'imprisons' adds to the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Danny is a male first name, so a man may be referred to by that pronoun.

clue.text: Catch son taking jade

parts.note: a jade is an old worn-out horse, a nag

explanation.surface: A boy is caught with a precious green stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Jade here is not the gemstone but an old word for a worn-out horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden drawback or problem, a hitch.

clue.text: Canned beef contains poison

indicators.note: contains says one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: canned food comes in a tin
beef comes from an ox

explanation.surface: Tinned meat is found to be poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a poisonous substance made by a living organism.

clue.text: It's imperative for French valley to retain it

indicators.note: to retain says the valley holds the word it inside

parts.note: val is French for valley

explanation.surface: It is essential that a French valley keeps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means essential or absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Fail to hang on to a hold-all

definitions.text: Fail to hang on to a hold-all

parts.words: Fail to hang on to a hold-all
parts.note: read straight it is about failing to keep hold of a travel bag, which in British usage is called a grip

explanation.walkthrough: A grip is an old word for a holdall or travelling bag, so the phrase for losing control also describes dropping one's bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose control or stop coping is idiomatically to let go of one's hold on things.

clue.text: Having fired one German worker, he's in court

parts.note: fired means set alight, lit
I is the Roman numeral one
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: After sacking a German employee, he finds himself at a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests dismissal but means set alight; 'worker' is the crossword ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigant is a party to a lawsuit.

clue.text: Waiters worked with energy in a way

indicators.note: worked says the letters of waiters are reshaped

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Waiters toiled energetically, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges WAITERS, then E for energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means so to speak, in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Caterers from Ireland I send off

indicators.note: off says the letters of these words go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food suppliers from Ireland being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges IRELAND I SEND. In Britain, dinner ladies serve school lunches.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, dinner ladies are the women who serve meals in school canteens.

clue.text: Spend one month in various places

parts.note: to spend time is to pass it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Use up a month travelling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is Latin for throughout, used in references to mean scattered through a text.

clue.text: Initial document again and quit

explanation.surface: Sign the papers once more and leave the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-sign is to put one's name to something a second time; to resign is to step down from a post.

clue.text: A mate filled with dread

parts.note: to mate is to pair up, as in to marry or wed

explanation.surface: A partner is full of fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in awe is a mix of reverence and fear.

clue.text: According to some in the Bahamas, perhaps

indicators.note: some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: How some folk in the Caribbean islands might tell it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft defined only 'According', but the phrase meaning the answer is 'According to'; 'the' is a link. 'some in' points to the letters ASPER inside 'Bahamas, perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: As per is a formal phrase meaning in line with or following.

clue.text: Roll and roll over

explanation.surface: A register, and a ship tipping.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a register of names, a list; to list is to lean over, as a ship heels to one side.

clue.text: A fish producing a gelatine-like substance

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish yields a jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly made from seaweed, used in cooking and labs.

clue.text: Transport stolen goods

explanation.surface: Carry off the loot.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul is to pull or carry a load; a haul is a thief's booty.

clue.text: "A painful disease," sighs Len, when poorly

indicators.note: poorly suggests something unwell, here the letters of the quoted words in a bad way

explanation.surface: Len sighs that he has an unpleasant illness while feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges SIGHS LEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingles is a painful viral rash caused by the chickenpox virus reawakening.

clue.text: May a primate eat it?

parts.note: may in the sense of being able to, can
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Is a monkey allowed to have this snack?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is both the wordplay and a playful definition: a cocktail snack that an ape might eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury bite served at parties, something to eat.

clue.text: Less than half are under eighteen

explanation.surface: Fewer than half of them are not yet adults.
explanation.definitionFit: A minority is the smaller part of a group; it is also the legal state of being a juvenile, not yet of age.

clue.text: Merry bachelor of lissom body

parts.note: of lissom body means supple, lithe

explanation.surface: A cheerful single man with a graceful figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means cheerful and carefree.
